title: MV Alnath Saga | Prologue | "J"RPG | Demo now available!

posts.author: Milthar
posts.body:
ALNATH SAGA PROLOGUE: DARKNESS DAWNS
A young prince is sent to investigate the disappearance of villagers.
What destiny awaits on that abandoned island?
​
SYNOPSIS
Two centuries ago, an evil wizard sought to seize the throne of the Kingdom of Alnath for himself.
Now, from the island on which he was defeated, a mysterious fog has suddenly appeared, and villagers have started going missing without a trace.
After the team sent to investigate also disappeared and with his attention focused on war in the north, King Ancelot du Alnath has little choice but to send his only son to investigate.
Now, Prince Conrad du Alnath, along with his bodyguard, Hildegard, and Cassandra, a magus from the college, who seeks her missing sister, must uncover the mysteries of that abandoned island.
CAST
Conrad du Alnath: The young prince and heir of the Kingdom of Alnath.
Hildegard Ingrahm: Childhood friend and bodyguard to the Prince of Alnath.
Cassandra Harrier: A college trained magus in search of her missing sister.
Julia Erlebald: A skilled ranger who used to be assigned to the missing investigation team.
IMAGES/SCREENSHOTS
Spoiler
ABOUT THE GAME
Alnath Saga is a high fantasy turnbased battle RPG.
Maturity Level/Warnings
Contains scenes of violence, blood, body horror, religious references. (Probably about a MA15+)
Length
The demo is about 1-2 hours long,
Containing 2 minibosses and 1 boss.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Although worded poorly, I think the point OneManIndie was making is that if your goal is to reach a wider audience of players, it would be a good idea to upload it through a service, such as Itch, where browsing and discovering games is easier.
I'm not particularly interested in playing your game. That said, I figured I'd at least provide feedback for how you market the game through it's pitch. You can take it or leave it.
Firstly: The title is both wordy and generic. The most interesting part is (I am guessing) the name of your world, Alnath.
So I would just retitled it to that: Alnath. No subtitle necessary. You could call it Alnath Prologue too. Saga seems unnecessary, it either is a saga or it isn't. You don't need to tell your players it is. Darkness Dawns is just meaningless and doesn't inform the player what the game is - it doesn't even really tie into the synopsis.
Speaking of the synopsis, there's a lot of unncessary world building that makes the game sound generic and uninteresting. Simply by cutting some information I think makes it much tighter and also less generic sounding. I would write it like this:
A mysterious fog has suddenly appeared, and villagers have started going missing without a trace.
After the team sent to investigate also disappeared, King Ancelot du Alnath has little choice but to send his only son to investigate.
Now, Prince Conrad du Alnath, along with his bodyguard, Hildegard, and Cassandra,, must uncover the mysteries of that abandoned island.
It's not perfect, there are some tweaks that could be made from there, but that, to me, sounds way more interesting then what was there before.
I removed the "Two centuries ago" because we aren't playing the story two centuries ago, we are playing whatever story is happening the present. This is unnecessary lore dumping in the synopsis which is suppose to hook the player.
This sentiment can be shared among many of the cuts I made, including removal of "from the island on which he was defeated" as it is more lore dumping that doesn't mean or matter at all to the uninitiated player.
"A mysterious fog" is a good starting hook beyond the typical "fantasy kingdom in turmoil" plot that's been done to death in fantasy RPG games.
Giving character motivations or other lore about the characters once again doesn't mean much to uninitiated players so it's just better to cut that.
Your game pitch matters because you're telling players why they should be interested in your game. Upon just reading the title, I immediately became uninterested in the game because it already sounded like a game I've played 200 times, and I felt that even more as I read the synopsis.
You can easily change players mood with a well written title...and the ability to discover it through high-trafficked websites.
Good luck!
